correctness.rationale: For binary linear 0^a 1 0^b 1 0^c, the known n and counts N_{ell,j} give polynomials F and G. Multiplication by (1-z)^2 yields exact identities 2z-z^(a+2)-z^(b+2)-z^(c+2)+z^(n+2) and z^(b+2)-z^(a+b+3)-z^(b+c+3)+z^(n+2). Truncation through r recovers B=b+2 exactly if B<=r, and the multiset of outer markers A=a+1,D=c+1 below r, while all other information is invisible. The iff profile-signature classification follows both directions. Counting unordered A,D by visible B, both-small, exactly-one-small, neither-small gives four displayed terms. For n>=3r-1 they are r(r-1),r(r-1)/2,r-1,1, totaling r(3r-1)/2; one-class deficit at n=3r-2 (r>=2); r=1 is correctly handled. Independent literal substring profiles and both-way signature tests confirm every n<=18, all r<=n; formula boundary checked to r=59. Full proof not inferred from testing.
